newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen rebounding. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen rebounding. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]

text.p: Polish shares extended their two-session fall but analysts said they were likely to rebound on Wednesday as prices of several stocks already seemed attractive.

"Some stocks, mainly those which are not overvalued and have fallen recently (corrects from "not fallen"), might rise, which could push the whole market up," said Bogdan Kornacki, a trader at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) brokerage.
Some analysts also said domestic investors were likely to start buying in expectation of possible growth in January, when they expect foreign funds to open new positions.

"Before the end of the year funds close positions to show profits but in January they open them again, and some investors want to be quicker and buy shares before prices rise," said Pawel Hominski, a trader at DM Magnus brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 32.5 points, or 0.2 percent, to 13,290.0, and turnover rose 10.9 percent to 84.6 million zlotys on both markets with 33 issues up, 29 down and 21 flat.
Some chartists said, however, that if the market extended its fall below 13,000 points it might mean the start of a deeper correction.
Analysts could not explain the scale of the 10-percent plunge in active trade by Tuesday's biggest loser, aluminium plant Kety.
Continuous trade turnover was at 14.6 million zlotys with four stocks rising and two staying flat. The remaining 15 stocks did not trade.
NFI units rose 2.6 percent in a 21-million-zloty turnover in continuous trade and rose 2.7 percent in 12.4-million-zloty turnover in the regular bourse session.
